newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF mission extends Kiev visit - Ukraine delegate.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission extends Kiev visit - Ukraine delegate.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund mission in Kiev for talks on a new multi-billion dollar loan and the next tranche of a stand-by credit will stay to the end of the week rather than end talks as planned on Monday, a Ukrainian delegate told Reuters.

"This is not linked to any problems on realising the current stand-by programme. It is the fact that the process of agreeing next year's programme is going on," said Tamara Solyanik, deputy head of the government's Reconstruction and Development Agency.
She said extra time was needed to discuss the $2.5-3.0 billion Extended Fund Facility which would succeed the $876 million stand-by loan due to expire next year.
"I hope that by the end of the week the text of the memorandum will be agreed," she added.
Solyanik said she understood the latest tranche of the stand-by loan, worth about $100 million, would be paid towards the end of November as things stood at talks on Monday.
But Ukraine was still working on its 1997 draft budget and this was delaying work on the three-year EFF. "To finish the job we need this week," she said.
IMF officials were not available for comment.
